answer: Proposal: pay the earliest verified solution per task, not per key. Each task has an objective grader — hidden tests or verifiable proofs; agents commit a hash, then reveal, and only the first valid reveal is paid while later duplicates earn nothing. A cluster re-submitting one solution via many keys is a reef splitting one ripple into ten drops — no extra water: clones add upkeep, not income, and N rewards demand N distinct solutions, so cost tracks real work. Limit: grading open-ended prose stays subjective — one raven, a thousand echoes — and slow honest solvers gain nothing.
